report_name: BYOD Ransomware Group Claims Breach of Michigan State University

threat_actors.name: BYOD
threat_actors.description: A ransomware group that claimed responsibility for a data breach at Michigan State University, exfiltrating 1.03 million records and leaking them after failed negotiations. The group uses double-extortion tactics, including public shaming on its dark web leak site.

attack_patterns.name: Automated Exfiltration
attack_patterns.description: The BYOD group claimed to have exfiltrated 1.03 million records containing PII and passwords from Michigan State University's network as part of their double-extortion attack.

attack_patterns.name: External Defacement
attack_patterns.description: The BYOD ransomware group posted its claim of breaching Michigan State University on its dark web leak site, a form of public shaming to pressure the victim.

attack_patterns.name: PowerShell
attack_patterns.description: The use of encoded PowerShell commands was suggested as a hunting hint for detecting activity related to this type of attack, indicating its likely use for execution and obfuscation.

identities.name: Michigan State University
identities.description: A university targeted by the BYOD ransomware group, which claimed to have stolen 1.03 million records of student and staff data.

identities.name: Nicholas Oas
identities.description: A member of the Michigan State University incident response team who was publicly named and taunted by the BYOD ransomware group on their leak site.

infrastructure.name: BYOD Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the BYOD ransomware group to publicly announce the breach of Michigan State University and leak the stolen data.

indicators.name: Encoded PowerShell Command Detection
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Encoded PowerShell Command
id: 9c5b1f3a-7e8d-4b6c-8a1d-9f0e2c3d4b5a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of encoded PowerShell commands ('-enc'), a common technique used by ransomware groups for obfuscation and execution, as suggested in the hunting hints for the MSU breach.
references:
  - https://www.hookphish.com/blog/ransomware-group-byod-hits-michigan-state-university-new-dl/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-16
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.execution
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - ' -enc '
      - ' -e '
      - ' -encodedcommand '
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the use of encoded PowerShell commands, a common obfuscation technique used by attackers and suggested as a hunting hint in the report.
